mainTopic: When blood of a חטאת makes a garment need כיבוס: blood that becomes פסול, disqualified offerings, and blood not fit for הזאה
overview: רמי בר חמא asks רב חסדא about blood of a חטאת that sprays onto a טמא garment, making the blood פסול at the very moment it lands. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע learns from the question that blood which was fit and only later became פסול does not need כיבוס, so the real doubt is about becoming פסול at the same moment. רב חסדא ties this to the מחלוקת between רבי אלעזר and the רבנן about מי חטאת that became טמא, proven from sprinkling a נדה. רבה says רבי אלעזר follows רבי עקיבא, who treats passing over a טמא place like resting there. אביי disproves this and explains רבי עקיבא's ruling about the jug over the oven as only a גזירה. He then says the real מחלוקת is whether we learn earlier טומאה from same-moment טומאה. רבא instead says they argue about whether הזאה needs a set amount. The גמרא then brings the ברייתא where the first opinion, רבי עקיבא and רבי שמעון argue about blood of a disqualified חטאת, with the פסוקים each one uses. A new משנה teaches that only blood received in a כלי and still fit for הזאה requires כיבוס, and ברייתות give the source from "אשר יזה".

steps.title: Blood that sprays onto an impure garment
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא asks רב חסדא what the law is when blood of a חטאת sprays onto a garment that is טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא asked רב חסדא: if the blood sprayed onto an impure garment, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא asks a question. Normally blood of a חטאת that sprays on a garment makes it need washing, but what if the garment was טמא?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the blood touches the טמא garment, the blood itself becomes טמא and פסול. So the question is whether the garment still needs כיבוס, even though the blood became פסול right as it landed.

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא מֵרַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: Rami bar Chama asked of Rav Chisda:
If it sprayed onto an impure garment, what is the law?
phrases.notes: "It" means the blood of a חטאת. The washing rule comes from ויקרא 6:20.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא מֵרַב חִסְדָּא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a garment that is טמא need כיבוס when blood of a חטאת sprays onto it, given that the blood becomes טמא on contact?

steps.title: Learning a rule from how the question was asked
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע infers that רמי בר חמא already holds this rule: blood that was once fit and then became פסול does not require כיבוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהושע said: since he asked the question this way, learn from it that if the blood had a time of fitness and then became disqualified, its blood does not require washing.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע looks at how the question was worded and draws a rule out of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רמי בר חמא asked about pure blood that lands on a טמא garment. He did not ask about blood that was already טמא before it sprayed. This shows he takes it for granted that blood which was once fit and later became פסול does not need כיבוס.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it / conclude from this
A period when it was fit

steps.confusionAlert: רב הונא does not answer the question here. He is only showing what the questioner already assumed, so we can see what the real doubt is.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:
From the fact that he asked it this way,
learn from it:
if it had a time of fitness and then became disqualified,
its blood does not require washing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a hidden assumption out of the wording of the question in step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood of a חטאת that was fit and later became פסול does not make a garment need כיבוס.

steps.title: The real question: one after the other, or at the same moment
steps.stepSummary: The question is sharpened. Does the rule apply only when the blood became פסול before it sprayed, or also when it became פסול at the same moment it landed?
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this rule apply only when one thing happens after the other, but not when they happen at the same time? Or perhaps there is no difference?
steps.whatsHappening: Building on step 2, the גמרא now states exactly what רמי בר חמא is unsure about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רמי בר חמא assumes, as step 2 showed, that if the blood became פסול first and sprayed later, there is no כיבוס. Here, though, the blood becomes פסול at the very moment it touches the garment. The doubt is whether that timing changes the law.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps there is no difference

phrases.english: This applies when one happens after the other,
phrases.notes: The two events are the blood becoming פסול and the blood landing on the garment.

phrases.english: but when they happen at the same time, not;
or perhaps there is no difference?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי מִילֵּי בְּזֶה אַחַר זֶה אֲבָל בְּבַת אַחַת לָא אוֹ דִלְמָא לָא שְׁנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the rule found in step 2 to state the exact doubt
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is blood that becomes פסול at the same moment it lands treated like blood that became פסול beforehand, so that no כיבוס is needed?

steps.title: רב חסדא: it depends on a known dispute
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that the question depends on the מחלוקת between רבי אלעזר and the רבנן, as רבה explains it and as אביי resolves it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: this is the dispute between רבי אלעזר and the רבנן, according to רבה, and as אביי explains it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא does not give a simple yes or no. He links the question to an existing מחלוקת, and the next steps will lay out that מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that another case also involves something becoming פסול or טמא at the same moment it does its job. How רבה and אביי understand that case will decide our case too.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: "He" is רב חסדא, answering רמי בר חמא.

phrases.english: It is the dispute between Rabbi Elazar and the Rabbis
according to Rabba,
and as Abaye explains it.
phrases.notes: אביי's explanation comes later on this amud, in steps 9, 11 and 12.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ פְּלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר וְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3 by connecting it to a known מחלוקת
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The answer depends on the מחלוקת between רבי אלעזר and the רבנן, as explained by רבה and resolved by אביי.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: impure purification water still purifies
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא: רבי אלעזר holds that מי חטאת that became טמא still purify, because we sprinkle them on a נדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: רבי אלעזר says: purification water that became impure still purifies, since they sprinkle it on a menstruating woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for the מחלוקת that רב חסדא mentioned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נדה is טמא, so the מי חטאת become טמא when they touch her. Yet they still remove her טומאת מת. From this רבי אלעזר proves that מי חטאת work even after becoming טמא, and the רבנן disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: Purification water mixed with the ashes of the פרה אדומה

steps.confusionAlert: Here מי חטאת means the water of the פרה אדומה. It has nothing to do with the blood of a חטאת offering from step 1.

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Elazar says:
purification water that became impure still purifies,
for they sprinkle it on a menstruating woman.
phrases.notes: This is a נדה who also has טומאת מת. The water becomes טמא when it touches her, yet it still helps.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the source of the מחלוקת referred to in step 4
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אלעזר, מי חטאת that became טמא still purify, as shown by sprinkling on a נדה.

steps.title: רבה: רבי אלעזר follows רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that רבי אלעזר holds like his teacher רבי עקיבא: passing a vessel over a טמא place counts as resting there. So the water was already טמא before it touched the נדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה said: רבי אלעזר said this following his teacher רבי עקיבא, who says that passing a vessel over an impure place is like having it rest there.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה explains why the proof from the נדה works, by tying רבי אלעזר to the view of רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone could object that the water only becomes טמא as it touches the נדה, at the same moment it purifies her. That would prove nothing about water that was טמא beforehand. רבה answers that according to רבי עקיבא, passing over a טמא place counts as resting there, so the sprinkled water was already טמא while it was in the air above her. So this is real proof that water which is already טמא still purifies.

keyTerms.meaning: Is considered as if resting there

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the link to our case. The difference between "already טמא before" and "טמא at the same moment" is exactly the doubt רמי בר חמא raised about the blood.

phrases.english: And Rabba said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּשִׁיטַת רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא רַבּוֹ אֲמָרָהּ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said it following the view of his teacher Rabbi Akiva,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: הַעֲבָרַת כְּלִי עַל גַּבֵּי מָקוֹם טָמֵא
phrases.english: who said: passing a vessel over an impure place
is considered as if it were resting there.
phrases.notes: So the water became טמא while still above the נדה, before it even touched her.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבָּה רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּשִׁיטַת רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא רַבּוֹ אֲמָרָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how רבי אלעזר's proof from the נדה works
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר follows רבי עקיבא, who holds that a vessel passing over a טמא place is treated as resting there. So the water was טמא before it touched the נדה.

steps.title: The משנה about the jug carried over the oven
steps.stepSummary: רבה brings the source for his claim that רבי עקיבא treats carrying over a טמא place like resting there. A person passed a jug of מי חטאת over an oven with a שרץ inside. רבי עקיבא says the water is טמא and the חכמים say it is טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: A person was standing outside the oven, and a שרץ was inside the oven. He stretched his hand to the window, took the jug, and passed it over the opening of the oven. רבי עקיבא says the water is טמא, and the חכמים say it is טהור. Here is what they argue about: רבי עקיבא holds that the jug counts as if it rested there, and the רבנן hold that it does not count as resting there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the source behind רבה's claim in step 6 that רבי עקיבא treats passing over like resting. It quotes the משנה and then gives רבה's reading of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The jug never actually touched the oven. It only passed over it. רבה says רבי עקיבא calls it טמא because he treats 'passing over' as 'resting on,' and the רבנן disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: An oven. Here it holds a שרץ, so its opening is a טמא place.
A dead creeping creature, which makes things טמא.
A jug. Here it holds מי חטאת.
It counts as if it were resting there.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna: He was standing outside the oven
and a creeping creature was in the oven,
and he stretched out his hand to the window
and took the jug
and passed it over the opening of the oven:
Rabbi Akiva rules it impure
and the Sages rule it pure.
And this is what they argue about:
Rabbi Akiva holds: it counts as if resting there,
and the Rabbis hold: it does not count as if resting there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the משנה that רבה relies on for his claim about רבי עקיבא.
steps.raayaObject: רבה's claim that רבי עקיבא treats passing a vessel over a טמא place like resting there.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in פרה about the jug passed over the oven with a שרץ inside.

steps.title: אביי objects: רבי עקיבא agrees sprinkled water stays pure
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a ברייתא: רבי עקיבא agrees that sprinkled water passing over a טמא earthenware vessel or a טמא bed or seat stays טהור. That does not fit the idea that he treats passing over like resting.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי objected: רבי עקיבא agrees that if sprinkled water passed over a טמא earthenware vessel or over a טמא bed or seat, the water stays טהור. This is because nothing makes things טמא above it the same way as below it, except an olive-size piece of a dead body and the other things that make טמא through a shared roof. This includes a stone with צרעת.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבה's reading of רבי עקיבא. He brings a ברייתא where רבי עקיבא agrees that water passing over something טמא stays טהור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי עקיבא really held that passing over counts as resting, then sprinkled water passing over a טמא item should be טמא. Since he agrees it stays טהור, 'passing over equals resting' cannot be his reason in the oven case. Only special things like a dead body spread טומאה upward through the air.

keyTerms.meaning: Something made for lying or sitting on, which can carry strong טומאה.
Things that make טמא whatever shares a roof or the air above them, like a dead body.
A stone with צרעת, which also spreads טומאה this way.

phrases.english: And Abaye raised an objection to him:
Rabbi Akiva agrees about sprinkled water
that he passed over an impure earthenware vessel
or over an impure item for lying or sitting,
that it is pure;
for there is nothing that makes things impure
above it the same as below it,
except an olive-size piece of a corpse
and all the other things that make impure by overhanging.
This includes a stone with leprosy!
phrases.notes: This line adds that a stone with צרעת also spreads טומאה upward, like a dead body.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבה's reading of the משנה in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that רבי עקיבא holds passing over a טמא place counts as resting there.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי עקיבא agrees that water passing over a טמא item stays טהור. That would be impossible if passing over really counted as resting.

steps.title: אביי's new reading: a rabbinic decree in case it rests
steps.stepSummary: אביי says everyone agrees that passing over is not like resting. רבי עקיבא's ruling in the oven case is only a גזירה, in case the person puts the jug down on the oven. With sprinkling there is nothing to fear, because once the water leaves the hand, it is gone.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: Everyone agrees that it does not count as resting. Here they argue about this: רבי עקיבא holds we make a גזירה in case he puts it down, and the רבנן hold we do not make that גזירה. And רבי עקיבא agrees about sprinkling, because once the water has left his hand, it has left.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי replaces רבה's explanation with a new one. The argument is not about whether passing over equals resting. It is about whether the חכמים made a protective גזירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the ברייתא fits. In the oven case, a jug in the hand might really be set down on the oven, so רבי עקיבא makes it טמא as a precaution. Sprinkled water flying through the air cannot be set down, so there is no reason for a גזירה.

keyTerms.meaning: We make a rabbinic גזירה, a protective rule.
In case it comes to rest there.
Once it has gone out, it has gone out.

steps.confusionAlert: Under אביי's reading, the water in the oven case is טמא only because of a rabbinic rule, not because passing over really counts as resting.
steps.whyThisMatters: This takes away the base of רבה's explanation of רבי אלעזר in step 6, so the גמרא must now explain that מחלוקת in a new way.

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
Everyone agrees that it does not count as if resting there;
and here this is what they argue about:

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא סָבַר גָּזְרִינַן שֶׁמָּא יָנוּחַ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva holds we make a decree in case it comes to rest,
and the Rabbis hold we do not make a decree.
And Rabbi Akiva agrees about sprinkling,
since once it has gone out, it has gone out.
phrases.notes: Once the water leaves his hand, it can't be set down anywhere, so there's nothing to worry about.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves אביי's own objection by giving a new reading of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the מחלוקת: a rabbinic גזירה instead of a principle about resting.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא treats passing a vessel over a טמא place like resting there.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone agrees passing over is not resting. רבי עקיבא only makes a גזירה in case the jug is put down, and this does not apply to sprinkled water.

steps.title: Then what do רבי אלעזר and the רבנן argue about?
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי עקיבא no longer holds that passing over is resting, the water sprinkled on the נדה was not טמא beforehand. So the גמרא asks what the argument between רבי אלעזר and the רבנן is really about.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר and the רבנן, what do they argue about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question that grows out of אביי's new reading. It sets up the next step, where אביי will answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה explained רבי אלעזר as following רבי עקיבא's rule that passing over is resting, so the water was already טמא before it reached the נדה. Now that אביי rejected that rule, that explanation is gone. The מחלוקת needs a new explanation.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar and the Rabbis,
about what do they argue?
phrases.notes: This goes back to their argument in step 5 about טמא מי חטאת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 9. אביי's new reading removes רבה's explanation of רבי אלעזר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A new explanation of the מחלוקת between רבי אלעזר and the רבנן, now that the water was not טמא before reaching the נדה.

steps.title: אביי: learning earlier impurity from same-moment impurity
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that they argue about whether we can learn one case from another. The first case is טומאה that came before the sprinkling. The second is טומאה that happens at the very moment of sprinkling, as with the נדה. The next step says which side holds which view.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: They argue about whether we learn טומאה that came earlier from טומאה that happens at that very moment.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a new answer to the question of step 10. The next step finishes his answer by saying who holds which view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a נדה, the water becomes טמא only at the moment it touches her, and it still purifies her. The question is whether this lets us say that water which was already טמא earlier also purifies. This connects back to the question in step 3 about 'before' versus 'at the same moment.'

keyTerms.meaning: We learn one case from another.
טומאה that came earlier, before the sprinkling.
טומאה that happens at that very moment.

steps.whyThisMatters: This is exactly the 'before' versus 'at the same moment' difference that step 3 asked about regarding the blood.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
About whether we learn impurity that came earlier
from impurity at that very moment, they argue:
phrases.notes: The 'very moment' case is the נדה: the water becomes טמא right as it touches her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מחלוקת is whether we may learn the case of earlier טומאה from the case of טומאה that happens at the moment of sprinkling.

steps.title: אביי finishes his answer: one side learns one case from the other, one side does not
steps.stepSummary: אביי completes his answer. רבי אלעזר learns one case from the other, and the רבנן do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: One Sage holds we learn one case from the other, and the other Sage holds we do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing אביי's answer from the last step. It now spells out which side holds what.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר says we can learn the case of טומאה that came before the sprinkling from the case of טומאה that happens at the moment of sprinkling, as with the נדה. So for him the water still works. The רבנן say the two cases are different. This answers רמי בר חמא's question in step 3. For רבי אלעזר, blood that becomes פסול as it lands is like blood that became פסול before, so there is no כיבוס. For the רבנן, the two cases differ, so the garment needs כיבוס.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not learn (one case from another)

phrases.english: One Sage holds we learn [one case from the other],
phrases.notes: This "one Sage" is רבי אלעזר. He compares טומאה from before the sprinkling with טומאה at the moment of sprinkling.

phrases.english: and the other Sage holds we do not learn [one from the other].
phrases.notes: This is the רבנן.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר סָבַר דָּנִין, וּמַר סָבַר אֵין דָּנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's answer from step 11 by saying which side holds which view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי אלעזר and the רבנן argue about, now that passing over is not like resting.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אלעזר learns טומאה that came before the sprinkling from טומאה at the moment of sprinkling. The רבנן do not.

steps.title: רבא says the real argument is whether sprinkling needs a set amount
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees with אביי. Everyone agrees we cannot learn one case from the other. The argument is whether sprinkling needs a set amount of water, which small sprinklings can add up to.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Everyone agrees we do not learn one case from the other. Here they argue about this: רבי אלעזר holds that sprinkling needs a set amount, and small sprinklings join together to make up that amount. The רבנן hold that sprinkling does not need a set amount.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different explanation of the argument between רבי אלעזר and the רבנן about the נדה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אלעזר, the first small drops on the נדה are not enough to purify her, so they become טמא when they touch her. Later they join with more drops and do purify her, which shows that water already טמא can still work. For the רבנן, the very first drop purifies her at the moment it lands, so this case teaches nothing about water that was טמא beforehand.

keyTerms.meaning: They join together (to make up the amount)

steps.confusionAlert: רבא does not disagree that רבי אלעזר and the רבנן argue. He only changes what the argument is about. It is not about learning one case from another. It is about the amount of water needed for sprinkling.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Everyone agrees we do not learn [one case from the other];
and here they argue about this:
phrases.notes: "Here" means the case of sprinkling the נדה.

phrases.english: that Rabbi Elazar holds:
sprinkling needs a set amount,
and [small sprinklings] join together to make up the sprinklings;
and the Rabbis hold:
sprinkling does not need a set amount.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אֲמַר: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אֵין דָּנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's way of explaining the argument and offers a different one.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי אלעזר and the רבנן argue about in the case of the נדה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They argue about whether sprinkling needs a set amount of water that small sprinklings can add up to. Everyone agrees we cannot learn one case from the other.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי: the argument is about learning one case from another. רבא: everyone agrees we do not, and the argument is whether sprinkling needs a set amount.

steps.title: Only blood of a fit חטאת requires washing a garment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a disqualified חטאת and brings a ברייתא. It learns from the word "מדמה" that only blood of a fit חטאת requires washing the garment.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: "A disqualified חטאת..." The רבנן taught: "Of its blood" means the blood of a fit offering, and not the blood of a disqualified one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה about a disqualified חטאת. It brings a ברייתא with a source from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the garment must be washed when "of its blood" lands on it. The ברייתא reads "its blood" as the blood of a proper, fit חטאת. So blood of a disqualified חטאת does not require washing.

keyTerms.meaning: "Of its blood" (the word in the פסוק)

phrases.english: "A disqualified חטאת..." etc.
The Rabbis taught:
"Of its blood"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:20

phrases.english: means from the blood of a fit [חטאת]
and not from the blood of a disqualified one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה, separate from the discussion of sprinkled water.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood of a disqualified חטאת that lands on a garment does not require washing, learned from the word "מדמה".

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: it depends whether the offering was ever fit
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says that if the חטאת was fit for a time and then became disqualified, its blood still requires washing. If it was never fit, it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: If it had a time when it was fit and then became disqualified, its blood requires washing. If it never had a time when it was fit and was disqualified, its blood does not require washing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא disagrees with the first opinion in the ברייתא and makes a distinction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion, like the משנה, says no blood of a disqualified חטאת requires washing. רבי עקיבא says that once the offering had a moment of being fit, its blood keeps the rule of washing even after it is disqualified. Only an offering that was never fit at all is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: A time when it was fit

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next part of the discussion. The משנה said there is no washing whether or not the offering had a time of fitness, so it does not follow רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
If it had a time when it was fit and then became disqualified,
its blood requires washing [of the garment];

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הָיְתָה לָהּ שְׁעַת הַכּוֹשֶׁר וְנִפְסְלָה –
phrases.english: if it never had a time when it was fit and was disqualified,
its blood does not require washing.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: הָיְתָה לָהּ שְׁעַת הַכּוֹשֶׁר וְנִפְסְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second opinion in the same ברייתא, disagreeing with the first.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood of a חטאת that was once fit and later disqualified requires washing. Blood of one that was never fit does not.
steps.whatToRemember: First opinion: no blood of a disqualified חטאת requires washing. רבי עקיבא: it does, if the offering was once fit.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: No Washing for Any Disqualified חטאת
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון rules that blood of a disqualified חטאת never requires כיבוס, whether or not it was once fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון says: both this one and that one, its blood does not require washing.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives רבי שמעון's opinion, which disagrees with רבי עקיבא from the step before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא split the cases: if the חטאת was once fit, its blood requires כיבוס, and if it was never fit, it does not. רבי שמעון does not split them. Any disqualified חטאת, in both cases, does not require כיבוס.

keyTerms.meaning: Washing a garment that blood of a חטאת splashed onto
Both this and that, meaning both cases are the same

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon says:
Both this and that,
phrases.notes: "This and that" means the חטאת that was once fit and the one that never was.

phrases.english: its blood does not require laundering.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אֶחָד זֶה וְאֶחָד זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opinion that disagrees with רבי עקיבא in step 15
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood of any disqualified חטאת, whether once fit or never fit, does not require כיבוס

steps.title: What Is רבי שמעון's Source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבי שמעון's broad ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי שמעון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what פסוק רבי שמעון relies on. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא uses the one word מִדָּמָהּ to leave out only one case, the חטאת that was never fit. רבי שמעון leaves out both cases, so the גמרא asks where his second source comes from.

phrases.english: What is the reasoning of Rabbi Shimon?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the ruling in step 16
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק teaches that neither kind of disqualified חטאת requires כיבוס

steps.title: Two Words Leave Out Two Cases
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון learns from two limiting words, אֹתָהּ and מִדָּמָהּ, each leaving out one kind of disqualified חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written "it" and it is written "of its blood." One word is for the case where it had a time of fitness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי שמעון has two limiting words in the פסוקים, so he can leave out two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each limiting word removes one case. One word removes the חטאת that was once fit and then became disqualified. The other word removes the חטאת that was never fit.

keyTerms.meaning: "It", a word in the פסוק read as limiting
"Of its blood", read as "some of its blood" and not all of it
A period when the offering was fit

phrases.english: It is written: "It,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:22

phrases.english: and it is written: "Of its blood" —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:20

phrases.aramaic: חַד לְהֵיכָא דְּהָיְתָה לוֹ שְׁעַת הַכּוֹשֶׁר.
phrases.english: one is for where it had a period of fitness.
phrases.notes: The גמרא doesn't spell it out, but the other word covers the חטאת that was never fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Two limiting words, אֹתָהּ and מִדָּמָהּ, leave out both kinds of disqualified חטאת

steps.title: רבי עקיבא Uses "It" for Something Else
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא does not use אֹתָהּ for blood. He uses it to teach that a pot where תרומה was cooked does not need scouring and rinsing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא? He reads "it" as leaving out תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רבי עקיבא does with the word אֹתָהּ, and it answers in the same short line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא already used מִדָּמָהּ to leave out the חטאת that was never fit. He needs אֹתָהּ for a different law: scouring and rinsing a pot where holy food was cooked. That word tells him תרומה does not need this.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce given to a כהן

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva?
phrases.notes: This is a short question: how does he read the word "it"?

phrases.english: "It" excludes teruma.
phrases.notes: He means a pot where תרומה was cooked doesn't need scouring and rinsing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רבי עקיבא does not learn from אֹתָהּ the way רבי שמעון does
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי עקיבא uses אֹתָהּ to exclude תרומה from the law of scouring and rinsing

steps.title: רבי שמעון Doesn't Need a פסוק for תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון holds that even קדשים קלים don't need scouring and rinsing, so תרומה surely doesn't. That leaves אֹתָהּ free for the blood law.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון follows his own view, since he says that קדשים קלים do not need scouring and rinsing, and all the more so תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי שמעון doesn't use אֹתָהּ for תרומה as רבי עקיבא does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי שמעון's view, a pot of קדשים קלים doesn't need scouring and rinsing. If those holy offerings don't need it, תרומה, which is less holy, surely doesn't. So he needs no פסוק for תרומה, and אֹתָהּ is free to leave out a disqualified חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning stated elsewhere
Scouring and rinsing a pot where holy food was cooked

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא: מִדָּמָהּ leaves out the חטאת that was never fit, and אֹתָהּ leaves out תרומה. רבי שמעון: both words leave out disqualified חטאת blood, because he needs no פסוק for תרומה.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon follows his reasoning, as he says:

phrases.aramaic: קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים אֵין טְעוּנִין מְרִיקָה וּשְׁטִיפָה –
phrases.english: Offerings of lesser sanctity do not require scouring and rinsing —
and all the more so teruma.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רבי שמעון does not read אֹתָהּ as רבי עקיבא does
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי שמעון learns the תרומה law by קל וחומר from קדשים קלים, so אֹתָהּ is free for the כיבוס law

steps.title: משנה: Only Blood Received in a כלי and Fit for Sprinkling
steps.stepSummary: Blood that sprayed from the neck, from the altar, or that spilled on the floor does not require כיבוס. Only blood received in a כלי and fit for הזאה does.
steps.simpleTranslation: If blood sprayed from the neck onto a garment, no washing is needed. If it sprayed from the corner or base of the altar, no washing is needed. If it spilled on the floor and was gathered, no washing is needed. Only blood received in a כלי and fit for sprinkling needs washing.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It lists cases where blood of a חטאת does not require כיבוס, then gives the general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood from the neck was never received in a כלי. Blood from the altar was already sprinkled, so its job is done. Blood from the floor was also never received properly, so it is not fit. The rule needs both conditions: received in a כלי, and still fit for הזאה.

keyTerms.meaning: The animal's neck, where it was slaughtered
The corner and the base of the altar

steps.confusionAlert: Blood "from the corner or base" means blood that was already sprinkled on the altar and then splashed off. It is not fresh blood waiting to be used.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ נִיתַּז מִן הַצַּוָּאר עַל הַבֶּגֶד –
phrases.english: MISHNA: If it sprayed from the neck onto the garment —
it does not require laundering.
From the corner or from the base —
it does not require laundering.
If it spilled onto the floor and he gathered it —
it does not require laundering.
Nothing requires laundering except
blood that was received in a vessel,
and is fit for sprinkling.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ נִיתַּז מִן הַצַּוָּאר עַל הַבֶּגֶד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה with more limits on the כיבוס law
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only blood received in a כלי and still fit for הזאה requires כיבוס

steps.title: Source: Blood from the Neck Is Not Fit for Sprinkling
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from "אֲשֶׁר יִזֶּה" that only blood fit for הזאה requires כיבוס. That leaves out blood from the neck.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: you might think blood that sprayed from the neck onto a garment needs washing. So the פסוק says "on which it shall be sprinkled." I only told you this about blood fit for sprinkling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives the פסוק source for the first case in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words אֲשֶׁר יִזֶּה tie the כיבוס law to blood that can be sprinkled. Blood that sprays straight from the neck was never received in a כלי, so it can't be sprinkled.

keyTerms.meaning: "You might think", which opens a mistaken idea
"The פסוק teaches", which brings the correction

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל נִיתַּז מִן הַצַּוָּאר עַל הַבֶּגֶד –
phrases.english: One might think that if it sprayed from the neck onto the garment —
it should require laundering?
The verse states: "On which it shall be sprinkled" —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:20

phrases.english: I did not tell you
except regarding what is fit for sprinkling.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: יָכוֹל נִיתַּז מִן הַצַּוָּאר עַל הַבֶּגֶד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the משנה's first case
steps.raayaObject: The משנה's ruling that blood sprayed from the neck does not require כיבוס
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 6:20, "אֲשֶׁר יִזֶּה", meaning only blood fit for הזאה

steps.title: Source: Blood Already Sprinkled Is Left Out
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא learns from "אֲשֶׁר יִזֶּה" that blood already sprinkled, which then sprayed from the altar, does not require כיבוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא taught: you might think blood that sprayed from the corner or base of the altar needs washing. So the פסוק says "on which it shall be sprinkled," which leaves out blood that was already sprinkled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא. It gives the source for the משנה's case of blood from the altar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same words, אֲשֶׁר יִזֶּה, now teach a second limit. The law covers blood that is still waiting to be sprinkled. Blood that was already sprinkled has finished its job, so it does not require כיבוס.
steps.whatToRemember: The words אֲשֶׁר יִזֶּה teach two limits. Blood that was never fit for sprinkling, like blood from the neck, is left out. Blood that was already sprinkled, like blood from the altar, is also left out.

phrases.english: It is taught in another baraita:

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל נִיתַּז מִן הַקֶּרֶן וּמִן הַיְסוֹד
phrases.english: One might think that if it sprayed from the corner or from the base
it should require laundering?
The verse states: "On which it shall be sprinkled" —
excluding that which was already sprinkled.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא אִידַּךְ: יָכוֹל נִיתַּז מִן הַקֶּרֶן וּמִן הַיְסוֹד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ברייתא gives the source for the משנה's second case
steps.raayaObject: The משנה's ruling that blood sprayed from the altar's corner or base does not require כיבוס
steps.raayaSupportSource: "אֲשֶׁר יִזֶּה", which leaves out blood that was already sprinkled

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: blood that spilled on the floor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of blood that spilled onto the floor. This opens a new discussion of that case.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'If it spilled on the floor, and so on.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting the next line of the משנה, about blood that spilled on the floor. This is a setup line that gets ready for the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the משנה taught that blood that spilled on the floor does not require כיבוס, because only blood received in a כלי and fit for הזאה does. Now the גמרא points back to the exact words of the משנה so it can look closely at this case. No new law is given here yet.

keyTerms.meaning: Spilled. The blood poured out of the animal's neck.
The floor, meaning the floor of the עזרה (Temple courtyard).
Short for 'וכולי', meaning 'and so on'. The rest of the line in the משנה is assumed.

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new ruling. It is only a quote from the משנה that marks the next topic of discussion.

phrases.english: If it spilled on the floor, etc.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from our משנה. The rest of the line is: if he gathered the blood from the floor and it sprayed on a garment, there is no כיבוס.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After proving from פסוקים that blood not fit for הזאה needs no כיבוס, the גמרא now returns to the משנה's specific case of blood that spilled on the floor.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's clause: blood that spilled on the floor and was then gathered up does not require כיבוס. Here it is only quoted to start the discussion.
